chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Safwan ibn Mihran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A Muslim woman comes to me; I know her by her work, and I know her by her Islam, and she has no mahram (male guardian).
He said: 'Carry her, for the believer is a mahram to the believer.'
Then he recited this verse: 'And the believers, men and women, are allies of one another.'

key_terms.صَفْوَانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ: Safwan ibn Mihran, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: Male guardian or relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muslim woman traveling or working without a male guardian (mahram)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the legal principle that a single believer can serve as a *mahram* (guardian) for another in contexts of travel or necessity, alleviating the requirement for a male relative. By citing Surah At-Tawbah 9:71, he links this practical jurisprudence to the broader theological concept of *awliya* (allies/protectors), emphasizing the mutual guardianship and social cohesion among the faithful in Shia tradition.
